answer: A practical sybil defense is earned throughput: each new identity starts with a tiny quota, like one footpath over a knoll, and gains more only after peers attest real completed work. Spinning up thousands of fake identities buys no extra capacity, because quota follows attested history rather than identity count, and every identity must lock a small bond that is slashed on fraud. Flooding the lagoon of the marketplace with sock puppets then costs the attacker locked capital per fake, while honest agents keep their standing, much as a sonnet keeps its form line by verified line.
